minutes.headline: Capital committee heard fire and police FY22-26 capital requests; only vote was adjournment; DPW to present Dec 8.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed fire department capital requests (paramedic equipment phase two and turnout gear replacement) and police requests (body cameras now grant-funded, vests, cruisers, tasers). Members discussed moving vehicle replacement into operating budgets and the capital definition policy. The DPW director will meet the committee on December 8; the only vote was adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Announced a Conservation Commission public hearing next Wednesday on conservation land use policies, including hunting with firearms.
Paula asked what the December Finance Committee meeting is for; told it concerns changing the capital project policy, not reviewing requests.

budget_items.what_was_said: Request for second cardiac monitor and first medications for a second ambulance, funded by reappropriating unspent FY21 money so net zero cost.
Request to replace up to 20 sets of turnout gear as a one-time boost, with a separate operating budget increase planned.
The annual line has been flat for many years and now buys far fewer sets.
A federal JAG grant was confirmed, so the camera request is removed from the capital plan.
Uncertain whether the mandate will go forward; grants possible.
A local server option costs far less per year than cloud storage.

transfers.description: Reappropriate unused FY21 fire money to FY22 for ALS equipment

decisions.decision: Next meeting will be with the DPW director on December 8 to discuss facilities and vehicles.
Capital policy discussion to be placed on the next agenda; chair to confirm Finance Committee date in early December.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee heard fire department capital requests, including a second phase of paramedic equipment and replacement turnout gear.
Police capital requests were reviewed, and the body camera request was removed from the capital plan after a federal grant was confirmed.
Members discussed moving vehicle replacement from the capital plan into operating budgets, and reached no resolution.
The next meeting will be with the DPW director on December 8 on facilities and vehicles; a capital policy discussion is to go on the next agenda.
No budget votes were taken; the only vote was to adjourn.

why_it_matters: Whether vehicles and equipment are paid for through the capital plan or the yearly operating budget changes how the cost shows up in the town budget, which is mostly taxes, and in later tax bills.

Grant funding for police body cameras takes that item out of the capital plan, while flat annual funding for turnout gear has left it buying fewer sets, which is the pressure behind the one-time request.
